intro_md: The author's revision of 30 September is the chapter. It's saved word for word in `Drafts/Chapter 7 - The Last Keeper (Draft 5, the author's revision).md`, and in house style (straight quotes, "any more") in `Drafts/Chapter 7 - The Last Keeper (Draft 5, the author's revision, in house style).md`, which is the base for this list. The author asked for Claude's six notes on it as a change list: "make 1-6 as a change list". Earlier rounds are in `Chapter 7 - Changes (combined draft).md` and `Chapter 7 - Changes (first draft).md`.

changes.title: His silence confirms it
changes.before: "I know how long I've been in there. A thousand years, Thaer. He told me." She waited for him to look at her. "I know Mother might not be there any more. But the elves might remember her. They might know what she found. I have to ask."
changes.after:
"I know how long I've been in there. A thousand years, Thaer. He told me."

She waited for him to tell her the old man was wrong. When he didn't, she drew a breath that hurt all the way in.

"I know Mother might not be there any more. But the elves might remember her. They might know what she found. I have to ask."
changes.why: Note 4: nothing showed Thaer confirming the thousand years. The earlier beat is back, and it replaces "She waited for him to look at her." His silence is the answer, and she has to breathe through it before she goes on.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for Claude's notes 1–6 on the revision as a change list (30 September).

changes.title: Why Thaer stays
changes.before: "I have to stay here and deal with Leorin. If I leave with you, he can send whoever he likes after you."
changes.after: "I have to stay and deal with Leorin. While I'm here, he can't send anyone after you."
changes.why: Note 3: if Thaer went with her, anyone Leorin sent would have to get past him, so leaving didn't expose her. His reason is that staying lets him stop the pursuit at its source.
changes.decision_note: The author asked for Claude's notes 1–6 on the revision as a change list (30 September).

changes.title: Her last words to him
changes.before: "Then why couldn't you tell me that?" Her hand tightened around the rail. "I waited for you all night, Thaer. I thought you could help me understand what was happening. I… I thought *you*, of all people, would help me."
changes.after: "Then why couldn't you tell me that?" Her hand tightened around the rail. "I waited for you all night."
changes.why: Note 2: the ending explained the hurt. The author's comparison praised "So was I" because the hurt "pass[es] through the dialogue rather than having the narration explain it". "I waited for you all night" answers his "I was waiting for Father" in the same way, and "He looked away" does the rest. The name comes out with note 1.

summary_md:
## Names that stay

- **Thaer says "Seralune" three times:** "Seralune.", "Come back upstairs, Seralune" and "Seralune—".
- **She says "Thaer" four times:** "Something happened to *me*, Thaer", "A thousand years, Thaer", "Come with me, Thaer. Please." and "Thaer? / Thaer, don't."
- **Cyrandor says "Your Highness" six times:** "I did", "Cyrandor", "That's how it was told to me", "I've served here all my life", "I wish I had an answer for you" and "Mending it".

Nereth's titles are unchanged.
